children: GoPro has agreed to merge with privately-held Starman Optical in a $285 million cash deal, pivoting the company beyond consumer hardware into artificial intelligence data center and defense markets.

Under the terms of the agreement, shareholders of the maker of popular action cameras and digital imaging software will receive $1.14 a share, subject to working capital adjustments, while retaining a 10% stake in the combined public company.
Shares were halted from trading Tuesday morning. The stock is down 38% since the start of the year to close on Monday at 88 cents. The stock is down 44% over the last 52 weeks.
The deal will also include a recapitalization program where GoPro's outstanding $92 million in debt will be repaid in full.
The combined company plans to leverage GoPro's portfolio of more than 2,500 patents alongside Starman's domestic manufacturing to produce U.S.-made optical transceivers.

GoPro will continue supporting its core consumer camera line, but will also begin to shift its growth strategy towards consumer, commercial and defense markets while investing in growth and onshoring the manufacturing of products for strategic markets.
